What do you know of the history of your squeaky bag thingy?

I poked around online when I first started playing for history stuff. I don't remember a lot of specifics, but I saw it claimed the bagpipe likely originated in the middle east and spread everywhere they traded. It certainly spread to a lot of countries, so that seems like a reasonable theory.

I've been posting a bunch of non-scottish bagpipes likely on v/bagpipes to show the diversity of the instrument. The appearance and sounds can be really, really different from region to region. I find it pretty fascinating.

The Scottish say they've had the great highland bagpipe longer than any official record of it can be found, though. I wonder if that's tied in with the ancient Piobaireachd music style, which translates to something like "what bagpipes do", but some people think the style originated with a hero and was transferred to bagpipe. Maybe when the Scottish met the bagpipe, it was just one of those love affairs where you feel like you've known each other forever.

I know bagpipes used to be made out of any convenient wood with a good tone, often things in the rosewood family, and around, say, the early-mid 1900s they were commonly made of ebony or cocus wood. Now those woods are rare and the sound of those pipes is highly sought after. Part of that's the age, too, drones that have been seasoned that long are supposed to have special tonal qualities and be harder to damage with moisture fluctuations.

They're usually African Blackwood now, but that wood hit the endangered species list last year, so the trend of using various woods is starting to come back. People are scoffing a little less at fully synthetic bagpipes, too.

And then there was the whole mess with England oppressing Scotland and their culture, and they finally gave them back their kilts and pipes in return for Scottish military regiments.

Bagpipes have a long history on the battlefield, too, and pipers served in both world wars. I saw a documentary where they tested and demonstrated that Scottish soldiers have more strength and endurance when played bagpipe tunes, even compared to heavy metal.

That's all I can think of right now, I'm sure there's a lot more cool stuff.
